{
  "draft": "Subject: Formal Dispute of Security Deposit Deductions — Noida @bhk

[DATE]

[LANDLORD NAME]

Dear [LANDLORD NAME],

This letter serves as a formal dispute regarding the deductions made from my security deposit following the conclusion of my tenancy at [PROPERTY ADDRESS], which commenced under the lease agreement dated [DATE]. The security deposit paid was ₹50,000.

I have reviewed the proposed deductions from my security deposit and find several items to be inconsistent with the terms of our lease agreement and the principles of normal wear and tear. I formally dispute the following deductions:

1.  **Wall Repainting (entire flat) — ₹18,000:** This deduction is disputed. Clause_2 of our lease agreement explicitly states that normal wear and tear, including minor paint fading, shall not be charged to the tenant. While full flat repainting after a one-year tenancy might exceed normal wear and tear if actual damage occurred, you have not provided any evidence of damage beyond normal wear and tear. Furthermore, no invoice or quotation for the repainting work has been provided, as required by clause_4 of the lease. Move-in Photo 1 demonstrates the initial condition of the premises.

2.  **Deep Cleaning — ₹6,500:** This deduction is disputed. Clause_5 of the lease permits cleaning charges only if the premises are left in an 'unusually unhygienic condition.' You have not provided any evidence, such as move-out photos, to demonstrate that the property was left in such a condition. Additionally, no invoice or quotation for the deep cleaning service has been provided, contrary to the requirement in clause_4. Move-in Photo 1 provides a baseline for the property's condition.

3.  **Broken Bedroom Wardrobe Hinge — ₹1,800:** This deduction is unclear and therefore disputed. While clause_3 allows for deductions for actual damage beyond normal wear and tear, you have not provided any evidence, such as move-out photos, to substantiate the claim of a broken hinge. Crucially, no invoice or quotation for its repair or replacement has been provided, as mandated by clause_4. There is also no move-in evidence specifically confirming the condition of this hinge at the commencement of the tenancy. Move-in Photo 1 offers general photographic evidence of the property's state.

4.  **Two Missing Keys — ₹1,000:** This deduction is disputed. Clause_6 of the lease explicitly states that the tenant shall return all keys before the final inspection. However, you have not provided any evidence, such as a move-out inventory report, confirming that two keys were indeed missing. Furthermore, no invoice or quotation for the cost of replacement or rekeying has been provided, as required by clause_4. Move-in Photo 1 is part of the initial property record.

5.  **Floor Polishing — ₹12,000:** This deduction is unsupported and disputed. Clause_2 of the lease explicitly states that 'ordinary flooring wear' shall not be charged to the tenant. Floor polishing is typically undertaken to address ordinary wear and tear that occurs over the course of a tenancy. You have not provided any evidence, such as move-out photos, demonstrating damage to the floor beyond ordinary wear and tear. Additionally, no invoice or quotation for the polishing work has been provided, as required by clause_4. Move-in Photo 1 documents the initial floor condition.

The total amount of deductions disputed in this letter is ₹39,300. Therefore, I request a full refund of my security deposit amounting to ₹50,000.

I expect a full refund of the aforementioned amount within seven (7) days from the date of this letter. Failure to respond or provide a satisfactory resolution within this timeframe may result in the escalation of this matter to the appropriate consumer forum or rent authority for resolution.

DepositBack helps organise evidence and draft communication. It does not provide legal representation and does not guarantee any outcome.

Sincerely,
[TENANT NAME]",
  "subject_line": "Formal Dispute of Security Deposit Deductions — Noida @bhk",
  "total_disputed_amount": 39300
}
